CVE-2026-105440.title: Switch Engine (EXOS) JSON-RPC Authorization Bypass Allows Read-Only Users to Disclose Sensitive Information
CVE-2026-105440.description:
Missing authorization in the JSON-RPC web services interface
of Extreme Networks Switch Engine (EXOS) allows an authenticated,
low-privileged (read-only) user to execute CLI show commands that are
restricted to that role through the command line interface. Successful
exploitation results in disclosure of sensitive information, including the
device configuration and the password hashes of local accounts. Configuration,
enable, and debug commands are not affected. Disclosed password hashes can be
attacked offline, and a weak password could lead to administrative access to
the device. This issue is fixed in Switch Engine 33.7.1-patch1-11,
33.1.100.133-patch1-9, and 32.7.4.15-patch1-11.

Extreme Networks would like to thank Toàn Lê (GitHub: https://github.com/toanln-cov) for responsibly disclosing this vulnerability and for working with our PSIRT team through coordinated disclosure.

CVE-2026-119328.title: Immich: Unauthenticated filesystem path injection (arbitrary directory write + recursive delete) in the machine-learning service
CVE-2026-119328.description: Immich is a high-performance self-hosted photo and video management solution. Prior to 3.3.0, the unauthenticated machine-learning /predict endpoint in machine-learning/immich_ml/main.py accepted an options object and passed its values into model construction in machine-learning/immich_ml/models/base.py without restricting security-sensitive parameters. An attacker with network access to the service could set cache_dir to an arbitrary writable path, causing model downloads to write there and causing clear_cache() to pass that path to shutil.rmtree() after selected model-loading failures. Depending on filesystem permissions and the selected path, this could modify files in mounted data locations or recursively delete an attacker-selected directory. The model-name allowlist prevents this issue from becoming arbitrary-model deserialization or code execution. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.0.

CVE-2026-99127.title: page_pool: keep frag_offset aligned for odd-sized requests
CVE-2026-99127.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

page_pool: keep frag_offset aligned for odd-sized requests

page_pool_alloc_frag_netmem() rounds the requested fragment size with

size = ALIGN(size, dma_get_cache_alignment());

dma_get_cache_alignment() returns 1 unless the architecture defines
ARCH_DMA_MINALIGN, which DMA-coherent architectures such as x86 do not.
There the ALIGN() is a no-op and pool->frag_offset advances by the raw,
unrounded size.

A single caller asking for an odd size then leaves frag_offset misaligned
for every fragment carved out of that page afterwards. The pool is shared,
so the damage is not confined to the caller that caused it.

The per-cpu system_page_pool used by generic XDP hits this.
skb_pp_cow_data() allocates its fragments with the raw packet length:

size = min_t(u32, len, PAGE_SIZE);
truesize = size;
page = page_pool_dev_alloc(pool, &page_off, &truesize);

leaving frag_offset odd for whatever is carved out of that page next.…

CVE-2026-99426.title: smb: client: hold server info until cifsd exits
CVE-2026-99426.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: hold server info until cifsd exits

The last session reference can be dropped while the cifsd demultiplex
thread is still running clean_demultiplex_info(). That thread frees
TCP_Server_Info there, racing with cifs_put_tcp_session() as it releases
the server crypto state. syzbot reported a KASAN use-after-free in
cifs_crypto_secmech_release().

Keep an object reference for the cifsd thread. Defer final crypto,
session-key, network namespace, string, and structure cleanup until both
the last session reference and the thread reference are dropped. Drop the
thread reference after clean_demultiplex_info() has finished using the
server.

Build-tested with ARCH=arm64 and W=1 for
fs/smb/client/connect.o. The KASAN reproducer was not run on the patched
kernel.

CVE-2026-99677.title: xfs: clamp the pNFS layout range to the maximum file size
CVE-2026-99677.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: clamp the pNFS layout range to the maximum file size

xfs_fs_map_blocks() lets two bad layout ranges through. An offset of
2^63 or more is negative and passes "offset > limit". A length above
the limit, such as NFS4_UINT64_MAX, wraps "offset > limit - length"
and stays unclamped. With NFS4_UINT64_MAX, a read layout is built from
an uninitialized mapping.

Reject a negative offset and one at the limit, and clamp the length.
This needs "xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one
extent".

CVE-2026-99743.title: ksmbd: grant a POSIX ACL group entry only to the group's members
CVE-2026-99743.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: grant a POSIX ACL group entry only to the group's members

When no ACE of the DACL matches the caller, Everyone or Authenticated
Users, smb_check_perm_dacl() falls back to the file's POSIX ACL. It
takes the first ACL_USER or ACL_GROUP entry whose id equals the
caller's uid. For ACL_GROUP, this compares a gid with the caller's uid.
A numerical match grants the group's permissions even when the caller
is not a member.

Match a group entry only when the caller is also in the group.

CVE-2026-99800.title: io_uring: free the task context after a grace period
CVE-2026-99800.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring: free the task context after a grace period

A task other than the owner can free a request, io_ring_exit_work()
running the local task_work of a DEFER_TASKRUN ring for example, or
io_do_iopoll() reaping completions. io_put_task() then takes the else
branch:

percpu_counter_sub(&tctx->inflight, 1);
if (unlikely(atomic_read(&tctx->in_cancel)))
wake_up(&tctx->wait);
put_task_struct(tctx->task);

The first line is what lets the owner leave io_uring_cancel_generic(),
and on exec it frees the tctx right after. Nothing holds that off for
the remaining three lines, the task reference only covers a tctx freed
along with the task_struct. It used to work out because
io_uring_del_tctx_node() took the uring_lock that the freeing side holds
across io_put_task(), until that moved to tctx_lock.

Free the tctx with kfree_rcu(), and enter an RCU read section in
io_put_task() before the count is dropped.
